newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch EU presidency holds talks on Albanian crisis.
newsitem.headline: Dutch EU presidency holds talks on Albanian crisis.

text.p: Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo, the current European Union president, was holding crisis talks on Albania with diplomats and advisers on Thursday, a spokesman said.

"The minister is in his room with crisis staff and is trying to keep up-to-date with what is happening in Albania," foreign ministry spokesman Frits Kemperman said. "They are monitoring the crisis minute-by-minute."

Van Mierlo, who visited Albania last weekend for emergency talks with Albanian President Sali Berisha, had telephoned EU foreign ministers including Germany's Klaus Kinkel, Britain's Malcolm Rifkind and Italy's Lamberto Dini to discuss options.

"All options remain open," Kemperman said, adding that the Dutch had also been in contact with NATO, the United Nations and the United States administration. Diplomats from Albania's neighbours Greece and Italy also met in The Hague.
"The minister is on stand-by to go again to Albania, though he is unlikely to go there today," Kemperman said.
EU foreign ministers are due to meet this weekend in the Dutch town of Apeldoorn for informal talks which will centre on the situation in Albania and other key foreign policy issues.
Albania slid further towards anarchy on Thursday as gunfire crackled around the capital of Tirana and authorities closed the main airport after a nearby military base was looted.
Former Austrian leader Franz Vranitzky was forced to delay a European mediation mission to resume efforts to end the chaos, but said he would try to reach Tirana later in the day.
Rebels have seized control of the south of the country in an anti-government uprising sparked by the collapse of pyramid savings schemes.
